title: Jenna, 30: The $12,000 Wedding on a Card

scenes.say: About $24,000. That's what Jenna's $12,000 wedding really costs.
It all went on a card at about 24%. That's roughly $240 of interest a month.
She pays $300, so only about $60 touches the balance.
At that pace, she's paying for almost 7 years.
Now add $150 a month to the payment.
Debt free in about 3 years, and interest drops from $12,400 to around $5,300.
Cooking in twice a week, two fewer subscriptions and selling the decor covers it.
Would you put a wedding on a card? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, before a $12,000 wedding becomes $24,000 paid.

question: Would you put a wedding on a credit card, or wait and save?
description: Jenna put a $12,000 wedding on a card at roughly 24% APR and pays $300 a month. That takes almost 7 years and about $24,400 in total. Paying $450 a month cuts it to about 3 years and saves roughly $7,000 in interest. Estimates assume a fixed 24% APR and no new charges.
